---
title: "Toward Reporting Standards for Methodological Research"
---
**Speaker:** Karoline Huth, Maastricht University

### Abstract {.unlisted .unnumbered}

The development of new statistical estimators and modelling frameworks is central to quantitative psychology. However, unlike applied empirical research, methodological contributions lack shared reporting standards. Consequently, essential information regarding assumptions, estimation procedures, scope conditions, and computational constraints is frequently either difficult to locate or presented inconsistently in a manuscript. This heterogeneity complicates comparability across newly proposed methods, increases the cognitive burden on readers, and may hinder cumulative methodological progress.

In the present study, we conducted a review of a subset of articles published in leading methodological journals over the past year, including Multivariate Behavioral Research, Behavior Research Methods, Psychological Methods, and Psychometrika. The papers were categorised (i.e., new methods, simulation studies, tutorials, reviews, other) and coded at section level using a proposed, structured framework covering core components such as problem formulation, conceptual introduction, model specification, assumptions and scope conditions, estimation and inference, theoretical properties, computational considerations, and relations to existing methods.

The results indicate substantial variability in how key methodological elements are reported. While most articles contain the necessary information, its location and structure differ widely across journals and paper types, and no journal enforces a standardised organisational template. Building on this review, we propose a reporting framework for methodological research presenting newly developed methods, simulation studies, and tutorials, outlining recommended core sections.
